title: Memphis Design — An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: Idea to system
scenes.purpose: Show a single idea (yellow hub sticker) spawning a linked Memphis network on a deep-indigo halftone field, with the headline card readable throughout the second half.
visuals: Stationary deep indigo #2A2D6E field with low-contrast #353A85 halftone dot grid
Cream dot block, pink stripe block, yellow navy-dotted quarter circle (stationary patterns)
Sticker nodes: hard navy offset shadow, white keyline, pink/teal/yellow fills, navy contour
Yellow title card with navy lettering, white keyline and hard shadow
White link lines, gold ring pulse, fixed-trajectory confetti

beats.development: Hub square (the idea) pops in with tilted elastic overshoot; title card sticker-pops in with tilt and settles upright; teal zigzag begins drawing.

Five nodes burst out of the hub to their positions in a stagger; white links draw hub-outward after each node lands; decorative triangle, outline triangle, ring, crosses and wave pop or draw one after another.
captions: AN IDEA / BECOMES A / CONNECTED SYSTEM

beats.development: System clicks: hub bumps, two gold rings pulse outward, confetti bursts and fades; caption slides up.
captions: Shapes meet. Lines link. It all clicks.

beats.development: Fully settled composition holds for reading.
captions: AN IDEA / BECOMES A / CONNECTED SYSTEM
Shapes meet. Lines link. It all clicks.

findings: Headline is legible from ~0.9s once the card settles, giving over 2s of reading.
Node, link and decoration entrances are staggered so no more than a few objects move at once.
All motion ends by about 2.55s; the composition is settled before 2.7s.
justifiedHolds: 2.45–3.0s final hold so the headline and caption can be read with the finished network.

notes: Silent preview: no soundtrack or effects.

No preview recipes were supplied; this refresh demonstrates the source-frame background lesson (dark indigo halftone field, gold ring pulse, white sticker keylines, hard shadows, confetti payoff) instead of the earlier cream poster.
Source subject, mascot, branding and lettering were not copied.
